name: Okunoin and the Eastern Side
tagline: Lantern-lit cedars and Japan's most sacred cemetery
description: The atmospheric eastern end of town, anchored by the vast Okunoin cemetery and its two-kilometer cedar avenue leading to Kobo Daishi's mausoleum. Hushed, mossy, and profoundly spiritual, it is the emotional heart of Koyasan and unforgettable at dawn or after dark.
pros: Access to Koyasan's most iconic site
cons: Somewhat removed from the town center

name: Danjo Garan and Kongobuji Center
tagline: The spiritual core and grandest temple architecture
description: The historic religious center of Koyasan, home to the Danjo Garan complex with its towering vermilion Konpon Daito pagoda and to Kongobuji, the head temple of Shingon Buddhism. This is where the mountain's founding heritage feels most present and monumental.
pros: Central to the major temple sights

name: Daimon Gate and the Western Side
tagline: The grand gateway and quiet forest edge
description: The western approach to Koyasan, crowned by the enormous Daimon gate that traditionally welcomed pilgrims to the mountain. Peaceful and less trafficked, it offers sweeping views on clear days and a fitting sense of arrival at the sacred plateau.
pros: Good starting point for pilgrim trails

name: Town Center and Bus Interchange
tagline: Shops, cafes, and the practical hub of the plateau
description: The everyday center of Koyasan around the Senjuinbashi area and main bus interchange, where the town's shops, cafes, and services cluster. It is the most convenient base for buses, meals, and supplies while staying within easy reach of every major temple site.
pros: Best access to buses and services
cons: Less atmospheric than the temple ends
Can feel plain compared to sacred sites
